examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.

examples.text: Сегодня у нас контрольная по алгебре.
examples.trans: Today we have a test in algebra.
Everyone thinks you're in the hospital.
He was admitted to the hospital.

examples.text: Все думают, ты в больнице. Откуда деньги?
examples.trans: Everyone thinks you're in the hospital. Where did the money come from?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.
The main thing is, you keep him at home.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

examples.text: Полина, доченька, ну не плачь ты. Найдём мы Лютика.
examples.trans: Polina, sweetheart, please don't cry. We'll find Lyutik.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'быть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forget', paired with 'забывать'.

examples.trans: Don't forget to wash the toilet.

examples.text: Сейчас будешь чинить трубу. И унитаз не забудь помыть.
examples.trans: Now you're going to fix the pipe. And don't forget to wash the toilet.

meanings.note: impersonal with dative: вам завидно = you're jealous

examples.text: Вам завидно просто! Она очень красивая.
examples.trans: You're just jealous! She's very beautiful.

meanings.en: to start working, to come on

examples.trans: He earned a lot of money.

examples.text: Не твоё дело! — Это моё дело! — Я их заработала!
examples.trans: None of your business! — It is my business! — I earned it!

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: when the exact choice doesn't matter; first part declines like какой

examples.trans: You see, we need some kind of fantastic version.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

examples.text: Пятёрка по литературе, пятёрка по русскому.
examples.trans: A five in literature, a five in Russian.

examples.text: Хорошо! Пятёрка по литературе, пятёрка по русскому.
examples.trans: Good! A five in literature, a five in Russian.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'car; machine' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?
I thought maybe you wouldn't see me.

meanings.note: praise, said to a man, woman or child

examples.trans: I see, I see, you're a hero. Well done.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
He owns his own meatpacking plant!
She got a job at the meatpacking plant.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
неделю = for a week; через неделю = in a week

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'навидеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hate', paired with 'возненавидеть'.

examples.text: Скажи мне в глаза. За что ты меня так ненавидишь?
examples.trans: Say it to my face. Why do you hate me so much?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'deceit, trick' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Нина, не слушай. Это опять обман.
examples.trans: Nina, don't listen. It's another trick.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'куда').

examples.trans: Where does that word come from?
Thief, thief. Where does that word come from?

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: as a conjunction: пока я сплю

meanings.en: to bribe, to buy someone off (fig.)

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.

пятёрка.gloss: five (top school grade A; five-thousand-rouble bill)

examples.text: Пятёрка по литературе, пятёрка по русскому.
examples.trans: A five in literature, a five in Russian.

examples.text: А ты нам про все пятёрки рассказала?
examples.trans: Have you told us about all your fives?

examples.text: Хорошо! Пятёрка по литературе, пятёрка по русскому.
examples.trans: Good! A five in literature, a five in Russian.

meanings.note: polite formula, at a door or before asking something

examples.trans: May we come in? Good day, sir.

meanings.note: ironic: Сталину расскажите = tell that to Stalin
also a Russian man (as a noun)

examples.trans: Russian. Orthodox. Never been in prison.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'покойно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Его не будет часа два. Вы спокойно всё сделаете.
examples.trans: He'll be gone for about two hours. You'll do everything calmly.

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'красть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to steal', paired with 'красть'.

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'school' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The children are going to school.

examples.text: Привет, молодёжь! Почему вы не в школе?
examples.trans: Hi, kids! Why aren't you at school?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
